“Baaloo Mein Dekhi Bihar Ki Rooh” – The Sand Art That Stunned Sonepur Mela Visitors

Bihar witnessed a moment of pure magic at Sonepur Mela, where one artwork made people stop, stare, and feel proud of their roots. The breathtaking sand art by Ashok Kumar, the renowned sand artist from Chhapra, turned the English Bazaar zone into a cultural hotspot overnight.

A Living Canvas of Mythology and Bihar’s Identity

Sonepur Mela has always symbolised culture, history, and devotion. Yet this year, visitors found something even more compelling. At the residential complex of DM Saran, Aman Sameer, a stunning sand sculpture drew long queues of curious onlookers.

Created by Ashok Kumar (Sand Artist, Chhapra), the artwork brought the legendary Gaj–Graah Yuddh alive. Moreover, it portrayed the ancient tale with gripping clarity. A fierce crocodile attack, a helpless elephant, and Lord Vishnu arriving with His Sudarshan Chakra—every detail felt real.

Although the scene is mythological, the emotions felt contemporary. People connected instantly, and many even said the artwork helped them relive a story they grew up hearing.

A Deep Cultural Message Hidden in Every Grain

The second section of the sand art added another layer of meaning. Naturally, Ashok highlighted the iconic symbols of Sonepur Mela—horses and bulls. These animals are not just part of Bihar’s trade tradition. They represent pride, heritage, and a bond that stretches across generations.

Additionally, Ashok shaped the Bihar map, the Saran district administration logo, the tourism department insignia, and the official Sonepur Mela emblem. Each symbol strengthened the cultural essence of the artwork. Visitors could instantly see how Bihar’s past and present coexist beautifully in one installation.

Teamwork Behind the Masterpiece

Although Ashok led the project, he did not work alone. Young artist Sonu Kumar played a crucial role. He supported the structure-building and provided creative inputs. As a result, the artwork stood out for both precision and imagination.

This collaboration showcased how Bihar’s young talents now work fearlessly alongside veterans, creating art that speaks globally. The energy felt refreshing, and many visitors shared their admiration on social media.

Why This Artwork Matters for Bihar

Bihar is often celebrated for its festivals, rituals, and traditions. Yet artworks like this remind us that culture grows only when artists receive space and recognition. Thankfully, Sonepur Mela offered that space.

Furthermore, this sand art became more than a display. It became a bridge between mythology, heritage, and modern Bihar. Visitors experienced emotion, nostalgia, and pride—all at once. And that is exactly what makes this artwork unforgettable.

People from Bhojpur have visited it for generations. Earlier, visitors even travelled by boats because no other options existed. However, things have changed beautifully. Now, families plan their trips days in advance, and they prefer the comfort, safety, and affordability of trains.

With so many options, every traveller gets a suitable route and timing.

The rush at Sonpur Mela grows every year. Therefore, this new railway plan will help manage crowds, improve safety, and support tourism.

Because of these special trains, planning a Sonpur Mela trip has become easier than ever.

content:
Revolutionising Bihar’s Land Survey: Free 3-Month Installation & Diploma Course Backed by Survey of India and Indian Institute of Technology Patna

Imagine walking through Bihar’s fields, riversides and mines — and watching precision technology reveal what the eye can’t. Right now, thanks to a new initiative, survey personnel in Bihar will gain that power. Indeed, the collaboration between the Survey of India and IIT Patna is set to transform how we map, monitor and manage land in the state.

Why This Matters for Bihar

Bihar has long faced challenges in land-management: changing river courses, flood threat, unauthorised mining, and outdated maps. So when the Survey of India offered a three-month free installation of a continuous reference station system, and IIT Patna hosted a workshop on geospatial data and land surveying in Patna, we hit a milestone.
The workshop, held in the state capital, brought together experts to discuss how survey technology can deliver fast, precise data — with accuracy up to three centimetres. This is a major leap over older methods.

What the Programme Offers

  • The Survey of India will provide free installation of the reference station system (for three months) as part of the campaign.

  • The diploma course (40–80 hours) will be run jointly by IIT Patna and Survey of India at low cost for land-surveying personnel.

  • The technology aims to expedite data collection without needing external reference. As Director Prof. T.N. Singh of IIT Patna explained: this system can monitor river water levels, mining activity, bridges and transport infrastructure.

  • With accuracy down to three centimetres, mapping and processing systems will see a quantum leap — aligning Bihar’s infrastructure and land-use monitoring with global standards.

Fields of Application – A Game Changer

Agriculture

When farmers and officials have extremely precise land and water-data, they can make smarter decisions — such as optimising irrigation based on exact field contours, or mapping soil changes.

Flood Management & Rivers

If a reference station sits on a riverbank, it can tell today’s water volume and estimate tomorrow’s. With floods frequent in Bihar, this tool gives early warning and stronger planning.

Mining & Sand Extraction

As the system monitors mining zones like sand-extraction areas, it can flag daily extraction volumes and prevent illicit operations. This makes the task safer, faster, and less labour-intensive.

Infrastructure & Environment

Bridges, roads, transport hubs, environmental studies — all benefit from precise geospatial data. For Bihar’s push to modernise, this is foundational.

How Survey Professionals Can Benefit

If you work in land-surveying, revenue, mapping or fieldwork in Bihar, this course and installation offer is a real opportunity. With the diploma from IIT Patna + Survey of India, you acquire recognised credentials. With reference-station technology you gain hands-on with next-gen equipment. And with three-month free install you can pilot and prove this in your region before full rollout.

What You Should Do Next

  • Look out for official notifications from the Survey of India and IIT Patna about the diploma course dates, eligibility and registration.

  • If you’re a surveyor or work in land-records/mapping in Bihar, register early: seats will likely be limited given the 40–80 hour duration.

  • Ensure your organisation (government or private) is ready to host/coordinate the reference station installation during the free-trial phase.

  • Place this in your development planning: mention how your district or field can leverage this tech for agriculture, flood-management or mining oversight.

Bihar Awaits Its Big Verdict

The air in Bihar is thick with anticipation. After weeks of campaigning, two phases of voting, and record-breaking participation, the Assembly Election results are just hours away. At the heart of this massive exercise are the Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trails (VVPATs), safely stored in strong rooms under three-layer security. Each machine carries the fate of 2,616 candidates, representing 243 constituencies across the state.

Chief Electoral Officer Vinod Singh Gunjiyal told Akashvani News that stringent measures have been taken to ensure transparency and fairness. He emphasized that every counting centre is under elaborate security arrangements, ensuring a smooth and safe process.

The Election Commission of India and the Bihar administration have worked hand-in-hand to guarantee that the voice of every voter is heard without compromise.

Bihar’s Record-Breaking Voter Spirit

This election has been remarkable not just for its numbers but for its energy. People from every corner of Bihar — youth, women, first-time voters, and senior citizens — came together to shape the future of their state.

Moreover, the enthusiasm seen in rural belts, towns, and cities alike showcases a shared dream — a better, stronger, and more empowered Bihar.

From Gaya’s determination to Darbhanga’s drive, every ballot reflects a story of hope. As the results unfold, one thing remains certain: Bihar’s people have already won by turning up in record numbers.

Tomorrow’s counting will not only decide the next government but also reveal what the people of Bihar truly envision for their future. The spotlight will be on key constituencies, political veterans, and first-time contenders who represent the changing face of Bihar’s leadership.

“Bihar Heroes on Track: Siwan’s Railway Workers Win Safety Star Award for Their Quick Action and Courage”

A Spark That Could Have Been a Disaster – Saved by Bihar’s Brave Railway Workers

In a state often defined by its resilience, Bihar’s Siwan district once again proved that dedication and alertness can prevent disaster. On July 9, when fire broke out near the railway tracks close to Panchrukhi station, Gatekeeper Dilawar Hussain noticed the flames and acted immediately. Without hesitation, he informed the railway control room and ensured that the track was secured before any train passed. His swift decision saved lives, property, and ensured the safety of hundreds of passengers.

This act of presence of mind didn’t go unnoticed. The North Eastern Railway (NER) recognized him, along with two other Siwan-based railway workers, for their exceptional vigilance and awarded them the “Safety Star of the Month.”

Honouring Bihar’s Safety Stars

On November 11, at the North Eastern Railway Headquarters in Gorakhpur, General Manager Uday Borwankar felicitated the awardees in a special ceremony. He emphasized that safety remains the top priority of Indian Railways, and employees who perform their duties with sincerity and promptness serve as true inspirations for others.

Among those honoured were:

  • Dilawar Hussain (Gateman, 83-C Siwan): Detected and reported the fire near Panchrukhi station on time.

  • Om Prakash Kumar (Gateman, 4-C): Found a crack in the rail weld between Amalori Sarsar and Hathua on June 29 and repaired it immediately using a jogul plate.

  • Nehal Ahmad: Alerted authorities about a rail fracture at Siwan Junction on August 25, preventing a major accident.

A Culture of Safety and Responsibility

Every day, thousands of trains move through Bihar’s railway network — connecting cities, villages, and livelihoods. Behind this smooth operation stand countless unsung heroes who ensure safety before speed. Their commitment transforms ordinary duties into acts of heroism.

General Manager Borwankar highlighted that “alert and responsible employees form the backbone of railway safety”, ensuring that millions reach their destinations safely.

More Than Just Awards — It’s About Awareness

These recognitions serve as a reminder that every alert moment counts. When employees take ownership and act promptly, they protect lives, infrastructure, and the reputation of the Railways. Bihar’s Siwan team has once again demonstrated that courage and responsibility go hand in hand.

content:
From Skills to Success: Bihar Adopts SVSU’s Game-Changing Model for Its Own Skill University

A Bold Leap for Bihar’s Youth

Imagine a university where students don’t just study—they learn, earn, and grow. Bihar is now turning this imagination into reality. The state government has announced plans to build its own skill university inspired by the Shri Vishwakarma Skill University (SVSU) in Haryana.

Recently, a three-member delegation led by Deepak Anand, Secretary of Bihar’s Labour Resources Department, visited SVSU’s Dudhola campus. The team explored the university’s dual education system that perfectly blends classroom learning with on-the-job experience.

This initiative marks a major step toward a more practical, job-ready education model for Bihar’s youth.

Why SVSU’s Model is Worth Following

Industry-Focused Curriculum

Unlike traditional universities, SVSU focuses 60% on practical training and 40% on theory. Students gain exposure to real industry environments while continuing their studies. As a result, they become more confident, skilled, and employable.

Furthermore, SVSU runs an Earn-While-You-Learn model. Students engage in paid industry training while pursuing academics, creating a perfect balance between learning and financial independence.

Strong Industry Collaborations

The Bihar delegation witnessed world-class Centres of Excellence established by Daikin India and Usha Sewing Machines at SVSU. They also observed innovative student projects in robotics, drones, automation, and electric vehicles.

Such partnerships ensure students acquire skills that are directly relevant to today’s industries. Consequently, the transition from college to career becomes smoother and faster.

Empowering Students Beyond Degrees

SVSU’s mission is not just to provide certificates—it aims to build career-ready and entrepreneurial youth. Each course aligns with the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF), ensuring national-level credibility and recognition.

Equally important, the university is transforming how people view vocational education in India. It is proving that skill-based learning can be as prestigious as traditional higher education.

What Bihar Stands to Gain

Firstly, Bihar has a young population full of ambition but limited by traditional education paths. The new skill university will give them a direct gateway to employability and innovation.

Secondly, industry-integrated education will help reduce the mismatch between academic learning and job requirements. Students will no longer struggle to find work after graduation—they will already be part of it.

Moreover, this model supports entrepreneurship. Skilled youth will not only find jobs but also create them, fueling Bihar’s local economy.

Lastly, it reflects a clear intent by the government to prioritize outcome-oriented education. Bihar could soon become a national leader in skill-based learning.

The Vision Behind Bihar’s Skill University

According to SVSU’s academic model, the proposed Bihar university will adopt:

  • 40% theoretical learning and 60% practical training in real industries.

  • Dedicated Centres of Excellence in futuristic domains like robotics, drones, and EV technology.

  • Scholarships for deserving students to ensure inclusivity.

  • Active collaboration with industry leaders for internships and placements.

  • A focus on transforming education from degree-driven to skill-driven.

This model has already proven successful in Haryana. Now, it could reshape Bihar’s educational landscape too.

Benefits for Students, Parents, and Industry

For Students

They will gain hands-on experience, industry mentorship, and early job exposure. Instead of waiting to “learn later,” they’ll start applying knowledge immediately.

For Parents

This initiative ensures their children can pursue education that guarantees employability and growth. It brings stability, confidence, and a secure future.

For Industry

Companies will have access to a skilled, job-ready workforce. That means reduced training costs and faster integration of new employees.

For the State Economy

By nurturing talent locally, Bihar can minimize migration, attract investments, and strengthen its industries. Ultimately, it will empower communities and boost economic growth.

The Road Ahead

For Bihar’s vision to succeed, several steps are crucial.
First, the government must establish strong legislation and a transparent governance structure for the new university.
Next, industries must actively engage to provide training and job opportunities.
Moreover, high-quality infrastructure and well-trained faculty are essential.
Finally, equal access must be ensured so that even rural youth benefit from this opportunity.

If executed effectively, this initiative could redefine how India views education and employment—making Bihar a pioneer in practical learning.

This decision came amid reports of heightened alert following a recent blast incident in New Delhi, prompting Bihar’s security agencies to remain proactive. Seven border districts — currently witnessing voting — are under strict monitoring, ensuring smooth conduct across polling stations.

content:
From Mithapur to the World: Patna’s New APEDA Office Powers Bihar’s Agri-Exports

Bihar’s farmers finally have global doors opening closer to home. With the new APEDA regional office in Patna, the state’s rich agricultural legacy is stepping confidently onto the world stage. This initiative promises direct support for farmers and exporters—turning potential into performance.

A Local Office, A Global Gateway

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) has now established its Patna base at Krishi Bhawan, Mithapur.
Earlier, exporters from Bihar had to depend on the regional office in Varanasi for certifications, export guidance, and documentation. Now, that long wait is over.

With this move, farmers gain local access to export certification, packaging standards, and real-time market intelligence. As a result, small producers can now reach international buyers without costly intermediaries. This step also aligns with India’s broader mission of making agriculture globally competitive.

Putting Bihar’s Signature Crops on the Global Map

Bihar’s agricultural identity is tied to its unique products—each with its own story. The GI-tagged Mithila Makhana, Shahi Litchi, and Katarni Rice are already recognized for their premium quality.
Now, these crops can find stronger footing in markets like the U.S., Canada, and New Zealand.

Recently, Union Minister Piyush Goyal flagged off the first shipment of seven metric tons of Mithila Makhana, worth ₹1 crore. It was facilitated through the Patna office—proving how access and infrastructure can transform rural economies.

Additionally, traditional exports such as Jardaalu Mango, Marcha Rice, and Tilkut are now being prepared for global markets. This office will guide exporters in packaging, labeling, and trade compliance—making “Made in Bihar” a mark of excellence.

Empowering Farmers and Strengthening Incomes

For local farmers, the new office is more than an administrative unit—it’s a bridge to prosperity.
They can now access training sessions, workshops, and export fairs organized by APEDA. Moreover, with quicker certifications, shipments will no longer be delayed for months.

This direct engagement helps in reducing costs, improving product value, and building market confidence.
For example, farmer cooperatives in Muzaffarpur and Purnea are already preparing for their first export-ready batches of Makhana and Litchi under APEDA’s guidance.

A Step Towards Sustainable Agri-Growth

Beyond profits, this development drives sustainable agricultural practices. Export requirements often demand better quality control, environmental standards, and traceability. Hence, farmers are being encouraged to adopt organic and residue-free methods.

Such standards not only improve the soil and yield but also increase market value abroad. Consequently, Bihar’s agro-economy gains both reputation and resilience.

Furthermore, as global buyers seek authentic regional produce, this initiative ensures that Bihar’s rural identity travels globally—preserved and proud.

The Road Ahead: Building Bihar’s Export Ecosystem

While the opening of this office is a big leap, consistent follow-up matters even more. Bihar needs:

  • More export-oriented Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs).

  • Cold-chain facilities and testing laboratories closer to production zones.

  • Skill training for youth in agri-marketing and logistics.

  • Stronger digital tracking for product traceability.

When these systems align, Bihar’s products won’t just reach foreign shelves—they’ll dominate them.

A New Dawn for Bihar’s Farmers

Take the story of a farmer from Darbhanga, who cultivates Makhana but once struggled to find fair buyers. Now, he can get his product certified in Patna, learn packaging standards, and send it overseas. For him—and thousands like him—this office means hope made tangible.

Step by step, Bihar is reclaiming its agricultural pride, not through slogans but through systems. And with APEDA’s presence in Patna, the world will soon recognize the quality that Bihar has nurtured for generations.

title: Discover how NIOS and IHCNBT are reviving Nalanda’s legacy in modern education
summary: Echoes of Nalanda: Where Ancient Wisdom Meets Modern Minds Centuries before global universities existed, Nalanda stood tall as a beacon of knowledge and intellectual freedom. Today, its legacy is making a comeback — not as ruins of the past, but as a living philosophy reshaping modern education in India. The roots of monastic learning stretch […]
content:
Echoes of Nalanda: Where Ancient Wisdom Meets Modern Minds

Centuries before global universities existed, Nalanda stood tall as a beacon of knowledge and intellectual freedom. Today, its legacy is making a comeback — not as ruins of the past, but as a living philosophy reshaping modern education in India.

The roots of monastic learning stretch back to Buddhist viharas from the 5th century BCE. These early centers of meditation soon became structured institutions teaching ethics, philosophy, and logic. Over time, renowned universities like Nalanda, Vikramashila, and Takshashila became magnets for scholars across Asia. Their approach was holistic — valuing moral discipline, intellectual debate, and lifelong learning — qualities still vital for modern classrooms.

Nalanda: The World’s First Multidisciplinary University

While earlier monasteries focused mainly on spiritual growth, Nalanda Mahavihara (5th–12th century CE) broke new ground. It offered a residential, organized, and secular curriculum that taught grammar, medicine, astronomy, mathematics, and the arts alongside Buddhist philosophy.

What made Nalanda revolutionary was its inclusive and dialogic learning model. Debates, discussions, and commentaries were central to its pedagogy. Students came from China, Korea, Tibet, and Southeast Asia — a true example of global education before globalization. Education here wasn’t about sectarianism; it was a pursuit of universal enlightenment blending faith and reason.

Modern Revival: NIOS and IHCNBT Bring Monastic Learning into the National Framework

In the spirit of Nalanda, the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS), in collaboration with the Indian Himalayan Council of Nalanda Buddhist Tradition (IHCNBT), has launched a landmark initiative. Their mission? To modernize and formally recognize monastic education across India.

Traditionally conducted in Bhoti, this system preserves Buddhist teachings and classical Indian literature — from Nagarjuna and Dharmakirti to timeless Sanskrit works like Ramayana and Meghaduta. Now, this intellectual treasure is being aligned with modern academic frameworks at the Elementary, Secondary, and Senior Secondary levels.

Rajeev Kumar Singh, Director (Academics) at NIOS, calls it “a bridge between ancient wisdom and modern opportunity.” He emphasizes that the initiative is not about secularizing Buddhism but about empowering learners and giving equal recognition to traditional knowledge in today’s education system.

Preserving Culture, Strengthening Identity

The IHCNBT, representing Buddhist communities across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and North Bengal, plays a pivotal role in this educational renaissance. For Maling Gombu, General Secretary of IHCNBT, the initiative is both patriotic and cultural. It strengthens India’s identity as the birthplace of great learning traditions and ensures that monasteries remain active centers of knowledge.

Today, 132 monasteries across the Himalayas have been accredited by NIOS, enrolling nearly 10,000 learners. This movement is not just an administrative reform — it’s a cultural revival. The Bodh Darshan initiative dignifies centuries-old Himalayan education systems, reaffirming India’s position as the spiritual and intellectual cradle of Buddhist thought.

Nalanda’s Spirit Lives On

As the world searches for balance between technology and wisdom, Nalanda’s philosophy offers a timeless solution — education that nourishes both intellect and soul. Its revival through NIOS and IHCNBT is more than policy; it’s a return to India’s roots in value-based, inclusive learning.

The win places Adani ahead of big competitors like Torrent […]
content:
A ₹30,000 Crore Spark for Bihar’s Future

Bihar just plugged into one of its biggest power breakthroughs yet.
Adani Power Ltd has clinched the 2,400 MW Bhagalpur (Pirpainti) project after a fierce bidding contest, emerging as the lowest bidder with a tariff of ₹6.075 per kWh. The win places Adani ahead of big competitors like Torrent Power and JSW Energy.

Since Bihar’s electricity demand is expected to double to over 17,000 MW by 2034-35, this project couldn’t have come at a better time. It promises to fuel both energy security and industrial revival.

Why This Project Could Change Everything

1️⃣ Meeting Bihar’s Rising Energy Needs

Bihar’s growth story often faces one recurring challenge — power shortage. However, this project aims to finally close that gap.
By generating 2,400 MW of additional capacity, the state can now ensure more stable electricity for homes, businesses, and upcoming industries.

Moreover, steady electricity encourages new investments in sectors like textiles, steel, and food processing, creating thousands of indirect jobs.

2️⃣ Massive ₹30,000 Crore Investment & Employment Surge

Adani Power plans to invest roughly ₹30,000 crore in the Bhagalpur project. As a result, this initiative will generate over 10,000 jobs during construction and another 3,000 permanent jobs after commissioning.

Additionally, allied industries — including logistics, retail, and housing — will benefit from the resulting economic ripple. Infrastructure experts estimate that every ₹1 crore spent in such projects generates 200–250 man-years of employment, driving both skill development and regional growth.

3️⃣ Transparent & Competitive Bidding

Transparency remained central to the bidding process. The e-bidding system ensured fair play among all four qualified companies.
Adani’s offer — ₹6.075 per unit (₹4.165 fixed + ₹1.91 fuel charge) — turned out to be the most economical. In comparison, Torrent quoted ₹6.145, Lalitpur ₹6.165, and JSW Energy ₹6.205 per unit.

Consequently, Bihar secured one of India’s most competitive power tariffs, particularly impressive given the recent rise in coal and logistics costs.

4️⃣ Location, Design & Timeline

The project will come up at Pirpainti in Bhagalpur district, using an ultra-supercritical 3×800 MW setup under the DBFOO (Design-Build-Finance-Own-Operate) model.
Furthermore, it will follow India’s SHAKTI policy for coal linkage, ensuring steady fuel supply.

The first unit is expected within 48 months, with full completion targeted in five years. Since the land was already acquired and remains state-owned, groundwork will begin quickly with fewer delays.

More Than Power: A Path to Bihar’s Industrial Revival

For decades, Bihar has lagged in industrial investment while other states surged ahead. Limited infrastructure and unreliable electricity discouraged private players, forcing workers to migrate.

Now, this mega project could begin reversing that trend. Reliable power doesn’t just light up homes — it powers dreams.
With this investment, Bihar’s manufacturing share could finally grow, and migration might gradually decline.

Experts often stress that per-capita GDP and power availability rise together. Thus, as Bihar lights up, its economy may brighten too.

Tackling Challenges with Transparency

While excitement runs high, some local concerns deserve attention. Reports have mentioned debates over land lease terms and environmental impact. Therefore, ongoing transparency and community dialogue are essential.

Importantly, officials confirmed that Adani Power will receive no special concessions and must operate within state guidelines. The project land remains government-owned and will return to the state after the contract term.

By addressing these issues responsibly, the project can set a new benchmark for ethical industrial development.

What It Means for Every Bihari

For ordinary citizens, this isn’t just a power project — it’s a promise.

  • For youth: thousands of new jobs closer to home.

  • For entrepreneurs: consistent electricity to grow their businesses.

  • For families: stable power supply and better living conditions.

Bit by bit, Bihar is rewriting its narrative — from power-deficit to power-driven, from migration to momentum.

“New Lifeline on Rails: Kolkata–Siwan Gets Two Unreserved Specials — Your Ticket to Home & Hope!”

A Journey Re-imagined: From Rush to Relief

Imagine escaping the stress of crowded travel and stepping into a train designed with your comfort in mind. That’s exactly what the Indian Railways has done by launching two unreserved special trains between Kolkata and Siwan. These new services promise smoother travel, easier access, and stronger connections. Moreover, they aim to manage passenger rush effectively while ensuring timely journeys.

Why This Move Matters

In recent years, passenger numbers between Bihar and West Bengal have risen sharply. Therefore, these special trains come as a welcome step. Not only do they increase capacity, but they also offer flexibility for those who travel at short notice.

Most importantly, this initiative shows that Indian Railways continues to listen to its passengers, adapting quickly to their seasonal travel needs.

The route covers multiple regions across West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Bihar, bringing together people from different walks of life. Additionally, passengers benefit from improved train frequency, which reduces waiting time and crowd pressure.

Pro Tips: Travel Smart & Stay Comfortable

By following these tips, you can make your journey both safe and pleasant.

Bihar’s Hidden Gem to Get a ₹50-Crore Makeover: East Champaran’s Historic Horse Race Pond(घुड़दौड़ पोखर) Set for a Grand Transformation!

A Forgotten Heritage Pond to Get a New Life in East Champaran

Once a forgotten landmark, East Champaran’s Horse Race Pond—locally known as Ghordodar Pond—is set to get a stunning revival. The Bihar government has initiated plans to transform this historic site in Padumker Panchayat into a world-class tourist destination.

The Tourism Department has approved ₹13.54 crore for the project and released the first ₹3 crore for the financial year 2025–26 to begin the work. The upcoming facilities include walking tracks, guest houses, parks, markets, a banquet hall, and even a water sports restaurant — all designed to boost local tourism and employment.

From Neglect to Revival: A Heritage Site to Be Transformed

For years, the pond remained neglected despite its historical significance. Earlier, the Water Resources Department sanctioned ₹10 crore for cleaning, deepening, and developing walking tracks. Now, with an additional ₹13.54 crore already approved and another ₹25 crore under process, the total investment is expected to touch ₹50 crore.

The project aims to make it a world-class tourist destination featuring motorboat rides, selfie points, and recreational parks. This is not just a development plan — it’s a revival of East Champaran’s cultural pride.

The Man Who Sparked the Change

The transformation journey began when Prakash Singh, grandson of former Bihar minister Rajendra Pratap Singh, wrote to Chief Minister Nitish Kumar highlighting the pond’s historical and cultural value. Acting promptly, the Chief Minister directed both the Tourism and Water Resources Departments to inspect the site.

Following their visit, East Champaran District Magistrate Saurabh Jorwal also inspected the area. Later, during his Pragati Yatra on December 24, Nitish Kumar officially announced that the pond would be restored and developed as a tourist destination. Soon after, tenders were issued, and the initial phase of renovation began.

Local Residents See Hope and Opportunity

The excitement among locals is growing every day. Residents believe that this initiative will restore Ghordodar Pond’s lost glory and bring long-awaited prosperity. The project promises to create employment opportunities for youth through boating, hospitality, and tourism-based businesses.

According to Panchayat head Nidhi Kumari, the pond is not only a heritage symbol but also a gateway to economic growth. She added that once the site is developed, it will attract visitors from nearby districts like Shivhar and Sitamarhi, as well as from Nepal. The project, she said, will turn the pond into a symbol of pride for East Champaran.

A New Chapter for Bihar’s Tourism Story

Bihar is reimagining its identity through tourism — and East Champaran’s Horse Race Pond stands as the next big milestone. This ₹50-crore initiative reflects Bihar’s broader vision to promote eco-tourism, cultural heritage, and rural development together.

When completed, the project will not only draw tourists but also transform lives, creating a sustainable model of growth that connects tradition with modern recreation.

summary: Bihar Votes with Heart: Record 64.66% Turnout Reflects a New Wave of Awareness Bihar made history today.With 64.66% voter turnout in the first phase of the 2025 Assembly Elections, the state witnessed its highest-ever participation in a state election. For a land often stereotyped for its politics, this number tells a deeper story — one […]
content:
Bihar Votes with Heart: Record 64.66% Turnout Reflects a New Wave of Awareness

Bihar made history today.
With 64.66% voter turnout in the first phase of the 2025 Assembly Elections, the state witnessed its highest-ever participation in a state election. For a land often stereotyped for its politics, this number tells a deeper story — one of awareness, change, and rising political consciousness.

From Apathy to Action: Bihar’s Voters Step Forward

According to the Election Commission, the 64.66% turnout surpassed all previous state records, beating the 62.57% turnout in 2000 and even the 64.6% seen in the 1998 Lok Sabha polls.
Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar expressed gratitude to voters and poll staff, acknowledging their role in this democratic celebration.

This surge comes after a special revision of the voter list, which removed 47 lakh names. Many critics argued the move would suppress turnout, especially among poor and marginalized communities. Yet, Bihar turned up stronger. The passion for change clearly outshined the numbers on paper.

A Closer Look at Bihar’s Political Pulse

Historically, higher voter turnouts in Bihar have signaled waves of transformation. In 2010, Nitish Kumar’s JD(U), allied with the BJP, won big with just 52.73% turnout.
In 2015, when Nitish switched sides to ally with Lalu Yadav’s RJD, turnout jumped by over 4%, and the alliance triumphed.
Five years later, he realigned with the BJP, and despite a slight increase in turnout, his party lost 28 seats — showing that numbers alone don’t decide the outcome.

Now, in 2025, the first-phase turnout is 7.37% higher than the 2020 overall average. That’s not a small leap — it’s a sign of re-engagement, especially among first-time and rural voters.

Anti-Incumbency or Reclaimed Trust?

Conventional wisdom says a high turnout often means anti-incumbency. However, Bihar’s story might not be that simple.
Across India, states like Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh saw higher turnouts but voted for the same party again. Bihar could follow a similar pattern — or rewrite its own.

For the Mahagathbandhan, led by Tejashwi Yadav, this turnout might be an encouraging sign. He’s contesting from his family bastion, Raghopur, which has consistently favored the Yadav legacy. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary (BJP) and folk icon Maithili Thakur, contesting from Alinagar, also drew heavy local attention.

Each ballot cast today carries emotion — frustration, hope, and belief — all stitched together into one powerful democratic act.

The Road Ahead: Bihar’s Story Isn’t Over Yet

Only 121 out of 243 constituencies have voted so far. The remaining half will go to polls on November 11, and results will be declared on November 14.
What happens next could redefine the political balance of Bihar.

But beyond parties and alliances, this turnout stands as a tribute to every voter who chose action over apathy.
Bihar is not just voting — it’s speaking. Loudly, clearly, and with purpose.

summary: Dawn of Democracy in Bihar Tomorrow morning, voters across Bihar will make their voices heard as Polling begins in the first phase of the Assembly elections. content:
Dawn of Democracy in Bihar

Tomorrow morning, voters across Bihar will make their voices heard as Polling begins in the first phase of the Assembly elections. In 121 constituencies spread across 18 districts, the state braces for a massive democratic exercise. Crucially, polling will start at 7 a.m. and conclude at 6 p.m., though in select areas — including Simri Bakhtiyarpur, Mahishi, Tarapur, Munger, Jamalpur and 56 polling booths in Suryagarha (Assembly segment) — the poll time has been curtailed to 5 p.m. due to security considerations.

The Numbers Behind the Vote

More than 3.75 crore electors will decide the fate of 1,314 candidates in this phase. Among them stand 122 women and one transgender candidate — Priti Kinnar of the Jan Suraj Party contesting from the Bhorey constituency in Gopalganj.
On the political front:

  • From the ruling Janata Dal (United) (JD (U))-led alliance, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is contesting 48 seats, JD (U) 57 seats, Lok Jan Shakti Party (Ram Vilas) 14 and Rashtriya Lok Morcha 2 in this first phase.

  • From the opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD)-led Mahagathbandhan: RJD 73, Indian National Congress 24, and Communist Party of India (Marxist Leninist) (CPI (ML)) 14. Meanwhile Jan Suraj Party stirs the pot with 119 candidates in this phase, shifting the usual two-front battle.

High-Stakes Contests & Big Names

This phase will determine the fates of 16 ministers from the current government. Among them 11 belong to the BJP. Prominent faces include Deputy Chief Ministers Samrat Choudhary (Tarapur) and Vijay Kumar Sinha (Lakhisarai).
In another arena, the Mahagathbandhan’s face, Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, contests from Raghopur for the third time. His estranged brother, Tej Pratap Yadav, enters on his own ticket from Mahua. Former health minister Mangal Pandey fights from Siwan, and JD(U)’s veteran seven-time MLA Shravan Kumar seeks an eighth term from Nalanda.
Even the cultural world turns political: folk singer Maithili Thakur contests from Alinagar; Bhojpuri actor-singer Shatrughan Yadav (also known as Khesari Lal Yadav) contests from Chapra.

Security, Logistics & Voter Readiness

Given the scale and stakes, elaborate security arrangements accompany tomorrow’s poll. The Election Commission of India has emphasised free, fair and peaceful conduct. In addition, voters are urged to check their roll status and ensure their EPIC/voter ID is ready — after the final voter list revision that preceded this election. More than ever, every vote matters.

Why This Matters

Firstly, the first phase sets the tone for governance in Bihar for the next years. Secondly, the huge number of women and marginalised candidates reflects a changing political landscape. Furthermore, the presence of third-front forces like Jan Suraj signals that voter choices may expand beyond the traditional two-bloc narrative. Put simply: this is not business as usual.

Your Role Tomorrow

If you’re a voter in any of these 121 constituencies:

  • Check your voter status today.

  • Reach the polling booth early and carry valid ID.

  • Encourage family, friends and neighbours to vote.

  • Stay calm, follow instructions, and remember this vote is your say in Bihar’s future.

And if you’re not in these constituencies, stay tuned. More phases follow soon as Bihar moves through this democratic journey.

It sounds unbelievable, yet doctors at AIIMS Patna turned this medical crisis into a story of strength, skill, and […]
content:
Miracle in Patna: AIIMS Doctors Remove 3.1 Kg Spleen From Six-Year-Old Boy in Record Surgery

Patna, November 4, 2025 — A six-year-old boy weighing just 18 kilograms carried a 3.1 kg spleen inside his tiny body. It sounds unbelievable, yet doctors at AIIMS Patna turned this medical crisis into a story of strength, skill, and hope.

When a Rare Disease Meets Unbreakable Spirit

The boy arrived at AIIMS Patna with a swollen abdomen and constant infections. After several tests, doctors found he had Gaucher’s disease, a rare genetic disorder. This condition occurs when the body lacks an enzyme called glucocerebrosidase, causing fatty deposits in organs such as the spleen and liver.

Over time, his spleen expanded to a shocking 30 by 20 centimetres, weighing 3.1 kilograms. It began pressing on other organs, threatening his life. At that point, surgery became the only option.

However, operating on a young child with such an enlarged spleen posed a massive challenge. Still, the AIIMS Patna team stepped up fearlessly.

The Expert Team Behind the Record-Breaking Surgery

The complex procedure was led by Dr. Amit Kumar and Dr. Amit Kumar Sinha from the Department of Paediatric Surgery. They were joined by Dr. Rashi, Dr. Digamber, Dr. Gaurav, and Dr. Saurav, who worked tirelessly to ensure precision at every step.

Meanwhile, Dr. Neeraj Kumar guided the anaesthesia team with steady expertise. Dr. Pratap Patra, a senior paediatrician, monitored the boy’s pre- and post-surgery condition carefully.

Together, these doctors turned an impossible case into a milestone in Indian paediatric surgery. The 3.1 kg spleen removal from a child of this age now stands as a record across the country.

From Pain to Recovery: A Turning Point for Bihar’s Healthcare

The surgery lasted several hours, but every second was worth it. The boy recovered smoothly and was discharged in a stable condition. His parents, once worried beyond measure, now call it a second chance at life.

This operation proves that Bihar’s healthcare system is evolving rapidly. Families no longer need to travel outside the state for high-risk surgeries. With experts like these, AIIMS Patna continues to strengthen faith in Bihar’s medical excellence.

AIIMS Patna: Shaping the Future of Child Healthcare

AIIMS Patna has become a symbol of hope and progress in eastern India. Each breakthrough reminds us that world-class care is possible right here in Bihar.

This surgery is not just a medical success — it’s a message of confidence to every family seeking advanced treatment locally. As Bihar’s healthcare infrastructure grows stronger, stories like these redefine how the world views the state’s capabilities.

summary: Patna’s War on Dengue: Patna Municipal Corporation’s 18,000-Home Daily Blitz to Defeat Mosquito Menace A City at War — And Everyone’s Involved Every dawn in Patna now begins with action. Streets echo with the hum of fogging machines, and residents watch as civic workers spray every corner. The Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC), under the leadership […]
content:
Patna’s War on Dengue: Patna Municipal Corporation’s 18,000-Home Daily Blitz to Defeat Mosquito Menace

A City at War — And Everyone’s Involved

Every dawn in Patna now begins with action. Streets echo with the hum of fogging machines, and residents watch as civic workers spray every corner. The Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC), under the leadership of Municipal Commissioner Yashpal Meena, has launched a war-level anti-dengue drive, reaching 18,000 homes daily.

Unlike previous seasonal clean-ups, this mission is intense, structured, and city-wide. Teams are not only eliminating larvae but also spreading awareness door-to-door. The aim is clear — stop dengue before it starts.

Coordinated Effort: 375 Teams, Two Shifts, One Goal

To ensure complete coverage, five anti-larva teams have been deployed in every ward. In high-risk dengue areas, ten special units now work round the clock. The teams check rooftops, pots, overhead tanks, and under-construction sites — all potential breeding spots.

Across 75 municipal wards, 375 teams operate in two shifts daily. They use Temephos for larva control and Malathion for fogging. Meanwhile, a special 500-metre perimeter is sprayed around every dengue-positive home identified by the health department.

This coordinated rhythm of inspection, fogging, and verification ensures that no neighbourhood is left behind.

Hospitals on High Alert

Hospitals, often overlooked breeding grounds, are receiving special focus. Dedicated workers visit PMCH, NMCH, AIIMS, IGIMS, IGIC, Gardiner Hospital, and Rajvanshi Nagar Hospital daily for spraying and fogging.

This hospital-level vigilance reduces infection risk for patients and frontline workers. Moreover, it prevents re-infestation from within high-traffic healthcare zones — a crucial step that strengthens Patna’s overall defence.

Vehicles, Zones, and Rapid Response

The civic body has also mobilised 57 fogging vehicles across six major zones:

  • Pataliputra Zone – 13 vehicles

  • Nutan Rajdhani Zone – 12 vehicles

  • Azimabad Zone – 7 vehicles

  • Patna City Zone – 6 vehicles

  • Kankarbagh Zone – 10 vehicles

  • Bankipur Zone – 9 vehicles

Every evening, these vehicles move through colonies, markets, and schools, ensuring consistent coverage. Furthermore, each team maintains a logbook for citizen feedback. Random verification calls confirm that ground operations match official reports.

If residents face issues, they can call toll-free number 155304, and a rapid-response unit reaches the location the same day. This real-time grievance redressal has made citizens active partners in the drive.

From Awareness to Action

While PMC’s machinery is vast, the true strength lies in citizen cooperation. Commissioner Yashpal Meena repeatedly urges residents to keep their surroundings clean and water-free. Stagnant water, even in a bottle cap, can become a breeding ground within days.

Therefore, small daily habits — covering tanks, cleaning trays, and removing puddles — directly reduce dengue risk. Additionally, responding to fogging teams and sharing feedback builds trust and helps improve the process.

Together, these collective actions transform awareness into sustained prevention.

The Bigger Picture: Patna’s Health Revival

Beyond dengue, this campaign reflects a changing mindset in Patna’s civic governance. It shows urgency, data-driven planning, and citizen-centric response — values that define a modern city.

From fogging lanes to verifying calls, every small act adds up to a safer, cleaner, and healthier Patna. The anti-dengue drive is not just a seasonal measure anymore; it’s a public movement that places health at the core of city life.

Be Part of the Movement

The fight against dengue needs every hand, every household, and every neighbourhood.
Cooperate. Stay aware. Stay proactive. Together, we can make Patna mosquito-free.

Golden Jubilee Reunion: When Patna Women’s College 1975 Batch Turned Memories Into Magic!

A Morning Filled With Nostalgia and New Memories

As the clock struck 11 a.m., Patna Women’s College came alive with echoes of laughter and excitement. The batch of 1975 returned home after fifty years — their eyes gleaming with pride, their hearts filled with stories untold.

The reunion at Veronica Auditorium wasn’t just another event. It was a heartfelt celebration of shared journeys, life-long friendships, and the power of women’s education. Principal Sister M. Rashmi A.C. welcomed the alumnae with warmth, presenting each of them with a rose. Soon, a soulful musical performance filled the hall, setting a deeply emotional tone for the morning.

 Looking Back: From Simplicity to Strength

Patna Women’s College has been a pillar of women’s empowerment since 1940. Although the campus has transformed with time, its spirit of excellence remains unshaken. The alumnae recalled how classrooms once echoed with ambition and laughter, shaping not just their education but their entire outlook on life.

Amrita Jaiswal, President of the PWC Alumni Association, delivered a moving address. She shared her fondest memories — library hours, cultural events, and the camaraderie that defined their days. Her words bridged generations, reminding everyone that learning at PWC is about more than books — it’s about becoming confident, compassionate women.

The Tribute That Moved Hearts

A special video presentation followed, showcasing the evolution of the college through five decades. Old photographs, glimpses of the first classrooms, and snapshots of the 1975 sports field played on screen. Many alumnae couldn’t hold back tears.

Sister Rashmi also shared the college’s journey — from modest beginnings to a leading institution in Bihar. The alumnae applauded as she reaffirmed PWC’s mission to empower women through education and community leadership.

Then came the emotional highlight. The former Premier and Vice Premier of the batch offered heartfelt tributes, while the Sports Secretaries were honored for their achievements. Souvenirs and handbooks exchanged hands, sealing the memories of a day that blended the past and the present beautifully.

 Voices of the Past: Stories That Still Inspire

When the microphone opened for personal stories, laughter and tears flowed together. Some alumnae spoke of their first day at college, others of teachers who changed their lives forever. Every story added another color to the canvas of PWC’s history.

As they toured the renovated campus — the upgraded labs, new library wings, and bright classrooms — nostalgia met admiration. The once small corridors now led to vast spaces filled with opportunity. And yet, the same warmth lingered in the air.

 More Than a Reunion — A Legacy Reaffirmed

This reunion wasn’t just about catching up after fifty years. It was a reminder of how powerful education can be when it nurtures values and vision. The alumnae left with souvenirs, but they also carried something deeper — a renewed pride in being part of Patna Women’s College’s legacy of sisterhood and strength.

title: OpenAI Offers 'ChatGPT Go' Free For 1 Year To Users In India From November 4
summary: India Steps into the Future of AI India just got an incredible surprise! Starting November 4, OpenAI will make its subscription plan ChatGPT Go completely free for one year. The offer applies to every Indian user who signs up during the promotional window. This isn’t a minor update—it’s a game-changing move. India is now the […]
content:
India Steps into the Future of AI

India just got an incredible surprise! Starting November 4, OpenAI will make its subscription plan ChatGPT Go completely free for one year. The offer applies to every Indian user who signs up during the promotional window.

This isn’t a minor update—it’s a game-changing move. India is now the second-largest market for ChatGPT and among the fastest-growing. OpenAI clearly wants to deepen its roots here.

Interestingly, ChatGPT Go was launched only a few months ago in August 2025. It was designed in response to feedback from users who wanted affordable access to AI power. Since then, demand has skyrocketed, pushing OpenAI to expand it across 90 global markets.

What Makes ChatGPT Go So Different?

To understand the buzz, it helps to see what ChatGPT Go actually offers.

Enhanced Features

  • Significantly higher message limits.

  • More image generation per month.

  • The ability to upload files for AI analysis.

  • Improved memory retention for smoother long conversations.

Together, these upgrades transform how people use AI—whether for learning, creating, or building projects.

 The Free Offer

From 4 November onward, Indian users who register within the limited window can unlock ChatGPT Go for 12 months at no cost. That means no monthly ₹399 subscription fees for a full year—an unmissable deal for students and creators alike.

Why This Matters for India

1️⃣ Affordable AI for All

Until now, many users couldn’t justify premium AI costs. Now, with ChatGPT Go free for a year, OpenAI has removed that barrier. As a result, more students, teachers, and freelancers can experiment freely with advanced AI tools.

2️⃣ Empowering Students and Professionals

Imagine a student in Patna using ChatGPT Go to draft essays and generate visuals without limitations. Or a designer in Bangalore creating concepts in minutes. This promotion will help every professional boost their productivity and learning.

3️⃣ Strengthening the “India-First” Approach

Moreover, this offer aligns with the IndiaAI Mission and OpenAI’s commitment to empower local developers. It also celebrates OpenAI DevDay Exchange Bengaluru, the company’s first-ever event in India.

4️⃣ Boosting Innovation Ecosystems

The AI industry here is expanding rapidly. By providing affordable access, OpenAI is encouraging innovation from small towns as well as tech hubs. This move will undoubtedly fuel India’s next wave of AI-driven startups.

Key Details and Tips

Still, there are a few things to remember.

  • You must sign up during the promotion period starting 4 November.

  • The plan includes higher limits but not unlimited access.

  • After the 12 months, users may return to the standard paid tier.

Therefore, it’s wise to register early and make the most of the free window. The sooner you start experimenting, the more you’ll learn.

How Bihar Can Benefit from This AI Leap

If you’re in Bihar, this announcement opens a world of possibilities.

  • Students can use AI to improve writing skills and project work.

  • Creators can generate reels, scripts, and visuals without extra costs.

  • Teachers can build interactive lesson plans in seconds.

  • Entrepreneurs can test marketing ideas or design posters instantly.

Through ChatGPT Go, advanced AI is finally within reach for every curious mind in the state. And that can spark a massive wave of digital creativity.

“Patna Rising: Multi-Modal Hub, Smart Vending Zone & Elevated Road Near Airport Set to Redefine the City’s Future!”

A City on the Move

Drive through Patna today, and you can feel the pulse of change. The capital of Bihar isn’t standing still anymore—it’s evolving fast. The city is preparing for a major transformation under Chief Minister Nitish Kumar’s Pragati Yatra on February 21, where projects worth nearly ₹1,350 crore will be launched.

Among these initiatives are a multi-modal hub, a model vending zone, and an elevated road near the airport—each one crafted to ease congestion and modernize city life. Together, they mark a turning point for Patna’s urban future.

Multi-Modal Hub: Where All Roads Meet

Patna’s upcoming multi-modal hub will unify the way people move. It’s designed to bring buses, autos, e-rickshaws, and inter-city transport under one modern roof.

The plan includes a multi-level complex near GPO, linked to Patna Junction through a pedestrian subway. It will feature digital displays, elevators, EV charging bays, and spacious waiting zones. Moreover, real-time coordination between transit modes will cut travel time significantly.

This is not just a structure—it’s a statement of intent. As traffic density grows, the hub will simplify commutes, reduce chaos, and create a smoother, greener mobility experience for citizens.

Model Vending Zone: Empowering the Heart of the Market

Patna’s streets have long been a mix of energy and congestion. Street vendors bring life to the city, yet the lack of structured space has caused frequent traffic snarls.

To address this, the administration is developing model vending zones that balance order with opportunity. Vendors will now operate from well-defined stalls with lighting, sanitation, and storage facilities. Additionally, proper footpaths will return to pedestrians, easing both movement and safety.

This initiative celebrates inclusivity. Instead of displacing traders, it integrates them into a cleaner, more organized ecosystem—preserving livelihoods while reshaping urban flow.

Elevated Road Near Airport: A Gateway to Global Patna

The new elevated road near Jay Prakash Narayan Airport is another bold step forward. With passenger traffic rising after the new terminal opening, this link will ensure swift and seamless access.

The project envisions a four-lane elevated corridor that cuts travel time from city centers to the airport dramatically. Furthermore, it connects to broader infrastructure goals under the Patna Ring Road plan, strengthening routes to Bihta and beyond.

For travelers, this means fewer jams and quicker routes. For businesses, it’s a sign that Patna is ready for global attention.

A Ripple Effect Across Rural Patna

While urban projects take the spotlight, rural Patna isn’t left behind. A new road will soon link the Bihta–Sarmera route with Daniyawan Top, improving inter-block travel. Local residents near Naubatpur have also been advocating for a flyover at Nispura Lakh—a long-pending demand that might finally see approval.

Additionally, large ponds and lakes are being rejuvenated under MNREGA and Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali Yojana, supporting both irrigation and ecology. These parallel efforts ensure that growth spreads evenly, not just within the city but across the district.

Why It Matters: Patna’s Image Is Changing

This transformation is more than construction—it’s confidence in motion. For years, Patna has battled the stereotype of being “slow to grow.” Now, these projects show a city stepping into its own, ready to attract investors, students, and entrepreneurs.

Every bridge, road, and zone adds a layer of pride. And as these developments unfold, they redefine Bihar’s identity on the national map—not as a story of catching up, but of leading ahead.

Be Part of Bihar’s New Story

Infrastructure isn’t just about concrete—it’s about community. When residents care, cities rise stronger. Patna’s ongoing projects prove that coordinated efforts between citizens, planners, and leadership can create lasting impact.

content:
“Patna’s Pink Revolution: Women Take the Lead as PMC’s ‘Pink Innovation’ Wins Global Spotlight at ICRS 2026”

Patna’s Women Power Takes Global Stage

Patna is making history — and this time, it’s women leading the charge. The Patna Municipal Corporation’s (PMC) bold initiative ‘Pink Innovation’ has earned global recognition, positioning the city among world leaders in women-led sanitation and sustainable urban governance.

The project has been officially selected for presentation at the International Conference on Resilient Systems (ICRS 2026), to be held in Delft, the Netherlands, in March 2026. This marks a major milestone for Bihar’s capital, highlighting its emerging reputation in waste management, gender inclusion, and city resilience.

The ‘Pink Innovation’ Model: A Blend of Dignity, Inclusion & Sustainability

At its core, Pink Innovation is not just about toilets or waste facilities — it’s about empowering women and redefining how cities think about sanitation.

Under this initiative, PMC has rolled out several women-centric sanitation projects designed to ensure safety, dignity, and participation. Among the most impactful are:

  • Pink Toilets: Mobile and permanent toilets exclusively for women, including changing rooms and Loo Cafés. These serve women during festivals, fairs, and public events — offering them clean, secure spaces when they need them most. Currently, eight Pink Toilets (four mobile, two permanent, and two Loo Cafés) are operational across Patna.

  • Pink Material Recovery Facility (MRF): A space that champions women’s role in waste segregation and recycling. This model not only enhances the city’s cleanliness but also generates formal livelihood opportunities for women in the sanitation workforce.

These initiatives strongly align with the Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban 2.0, supporting India’s march toward Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) focused on sanitation, gender equality, and environmental sustainability.

From Local Innovation to Global Recognition

Speaking on the achievement, Municipal Commissioner Yashpal Meena said,

“It is a matter of pride for Patna Municipal Corporation. Our ‘Pink Innovation’ initiative has not only redefined sanitation in the city but also empowered women and strengthened our commitment to sustainable development. Representing India at Delft is a great honour.”

This recognition places Patna on the global map of urban innovation. Moreover, the Pink Innovation model is now being replicated by other city corporations across India, serving as a blueprint for inclusive and sustainable governance.

The story of Patna’s women-led sanitation revolution reflects what happens when innovation meets empathy, and governance meets grassroots empowerment.

Bihar’s Pride on a Global Platform

Patna’s Pink Innovation showcases how local governance, when driven by inclusion, can inspire global admiration. It’s not just about infrastructure; it’s about changing mindsets, building systems that value women’s leadership, and creating spaces that reflect equality and respect.

As Patna prepares to present its story at ICRS 2026, it carries with it the voice of countless women who turned challenges into change.

title: Bihar EOU blocks over 20,000 mobile numbers in cybercrime crackdown
summary: A Digital Tsunami Hits Bihar The digital storm landed hard in Bihar—and this time, it wasn’t business as usual. The Economic Offences Unit (EOU) has deactivated over 20,000 mobile numbers, blocked more than 13,000 IMEIs, and frozen crores in bank accounts to clamp down on cybercrime. This decisive action shows Bihar is no longer a […]
content:
A Digital Tsunami Hits Bihar

The digital storm landed hard in Bihar—and this time, it wasn’t business as usual. The Economic Offences Unit (EOU) has deactivated over 20,000 mobile numbers, blocked more than 13,000 IMEIs, and frozen crores in bank accounts to clamp down on cybercrime. This decisive action shows Bihar is no longer a passive victim—it’s fighting back with precision and purpose.

Inside the Crackdown: The Numbers Tell a Story

From January to September 2025, Bihar logged around 74,000 online fraud complaints. The EOU responded decisively, freezing ₹75.92 crore—just over 21% of reported losses—and returning ₹5.14 crore to victims.

In October alone, 249 mobile numbers linked to online scams were deactivated. The department has also begun a rigorous investigation into “mule accounts,” which are bank accounts used to launder fraudulent money. In August, officials flagged nearly 200 such accounts and retrieved information on 138 of them through national data systems.

Furthermore, over 513 social media posts and profiles spreading misinformation or promoting scams have been removed. Every measure adds another layer of protection for Bihar’s digital citizens.

Why This Crackdown Matters

1. Rising Threats in the Digital Era

Bihar’s growing internet reach has brought new challenges. While access improves lives, it also exposes users to phishing, fake investment schemes, and online job scams. Many victims come from semi-urban and rural backgrounds, where digital literacy remains low.

2. A Statewide Impact

Cybercrime isn’t confined to Patna or urban centers. Small towns and villages have also faced the brunt of fraudsters targeting unsuspecting users. This crackdown sends a clear message—no corner of Bihar is off the radar.

3. Building Digital Trust

The EOU’s ongoing actions reinforce public faith in the system. By tracking transactions, blocking devices, and freezing suspicious accounts, authorities are restoring confidence in online financial activity and digital safety.

Step-by-Step: How the EOU Is Winning the Battle

  • Mobile number blocking: Over 20,000 SIM cards linked to scams deactivated.

  • IMEI lockdown: More than 13,000 mobile devices rendered unusable.

  • Mule account investigation: Hundreds of suspicious bank accounts flagged and data retrieved.

  • Fund recovery: ₹75.92 crore frozen, ₹5.14 crore already returned to victims.

  • Social media monitoring: Over 500 misleading profiles and posts removed.

Each of these steps pushes Bihar closer to a secure and accountable digital space.

What It Means for Citizens

Every digital user in Bihar plays a role in this transformation. Awareness and caution are now vital weapons. Avoid sharing OTPs, clicking unknown links, or trusting random investment calls. If a message or transaction feels suspicious, report it immediately.

This campaign proves something powerful—when technology is misused, Bihar will act. With the EOU leading from the front, the message is unmistakable: cybercriminals can no longer hide behind screens.

title: Patna Physician Unveils Doxycycline’s STI Prevention Potential at IDWeek, Atlanta
summary: A Bold Statement from Patna on the Global Health Stage The moment felt electric: a senior physician from Patna walked into the room in Atlanta and declared that a 70-year-old generic antibiotic might soon shift the dynamics of STI prevention. At IDWeek 2025, a global infectious-disease gathering, he presented emerging evidence that using Doxycycline after […]
content:
A Bold Statement from Patna on the Global Health Stage

The moment felt electric: a senior physician from Patna walked into the room in Atlanta and declared that a 70-year-old generic antibiotic might soon shift the dynamics of STI prevention. At IDWeek 2025, a global infectious-disease gathering, he presented emerging evidence that using Doxycycline after sexual exposure—or in some trials before high-risk contact—can sharply cut rates of bacterial STIs like syphilis and chlamydia. According to his summary of international data, reductions of 80% or more are becoming plausible.

In fact, one real-world study found reductions of 86.4% for syphilis and 89.7% for chlamydia when doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (doxy-PEP) was used.

Yet, as the Patna physician emphasised, this is not a silver bullet. He stressed the need for medical supervision, regular STI testing, and antibiotic resistance monitoring. After all, the global agency World Health Organization (WHO) in 2025 explicitly began developing guidelines on doxycycline prophylaxis for STIs.

What the Evidence Shows — And Why It’s Ground-Shifting

Emerging Data.
Several studies now support the idea that doxycycline taken within 72 hours of unprotected sex can dramatically reduce certain bacterial STI risks. In one randomized trial among men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women, incidence of syphilis, chlamydia and gonorrhoea dropped significantly. Infectious Diseases Society of America Another real-world dataset supported these findings.

Key Findings:

  • Reduction in syphilis and chlamydia cases reached up to ~80-90% in some cohorts.

  • Effect on gonorrhoea is more modest and currently under question.

  • The WHO is reviewing and considering formal guideline development for doxycycline prophylaxis in STIs.

Why It Matters.
In many countries—including India—the burden of bacterial STIs remains high, yet prevention tools have stagnated. Here, an age-old antibiotic repurposed for prophylaxis could be a game-changer. Moreover, having a physician from Patna bring these results to a major international conference underscores how local expertise is now emerging as global voice.

From Patna to Atlanta: A Spotlight on the Physician’s Role

Diwakar Tejaswi (Senior Physician, Patna) took the stage in Atlanta and framed the data through a global-local lens. He argued that while the trials were conducted in Western countries and among high-risk groups, the findings have relevance for India as well—especially for populations that face educational or access barriers.

Importantly, Dr Tejaswi stressed responsibility:

“While doxycycline shows promise, responsible usage and ongoing research are essential to prevent resistance and ensure patient safety.”

That message resonates particularly in India, where antibiotic misuse remains high and resistance trends are well-documented.

Opportunities for India — With Clear Caution Flags

Potential Pathways:

  • Indian clinicians could consider doxy-PEP for high-risk individuals under supervised protocols.

  • Public-health authorities might integrate doxycycline prophylaxis into broader STI‐control guidelines if further Indian trials validate efficacy and safety.

But Important Caveats:

  • Antibiotic resistance is a real threat. Studies show that tetracycline-class resistance genes increased among microbes exposed to doxy-PEP.

  • Gonorrhoea remains hard to prevent via doxy-PEP and demands other strategies.

  • Any rollout must include STI testing, resistance surveillance, and patient education.

Watch This Space: What Comes Next?

With the WHO gearing up to issue formal guidelines on doxycycline prophylaxis in STIs, global public-health practice may soon shift.  Meanwhile, the presentation at IDWeek 2025 by a Patna physician connects global research to Indian relevance, potentially opening doors for local research, policy discussions and public-health dialogue.

title: Bihar to launch AI & Semiconductor Cluster
summary: A Fresh Horizon for Bihar Imagine a future where your home state becomes a tech-hub, where chips, AI labs and high-end manufacturing don’t just lie in the big metros—but bloom right here. That’s exactly what Bihar’s announcement signals. On 28 October 2025, CM Nitish Kumar declared that Bihar will host clusters for artificial intelligence (AI) […]
content:
A Fresh Horizon for Bihar

Imagine a future where your home state becomes a tech-hub, where chips, AI labs and high-end manufacturing don’t just lie in the big metros—but bloom right here. That’s exactly what Bihar’s announcement signals. On 28 October 2025, CM Nitish Kumar declared that Bihar will host clusters for artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor manufacturing—mirroring the ambitions of states like Odisha, Karnataka and Gujarat. 
This isn’t just another statement. It marks a turning point, especially for a generation that has watched so many migrate for opportunity.

Why This Matters

Industrial leap

By launching AI and semiconductor clusters, Bihar takes a bold step into high-tech manufacturing. As the announcement explains, the state will tie up with the Centre’s “India Semiconductor Mission” for chip manufacturing, packaging and design units.
Such industries require clean power, efficient water, skilled labour—all elements the CM claims Bihar now possesses.
Thus, Bihar shifts from being perceived only as a labour-supplier to becoming a manufacturer and innovator.

Massive jobs & livelihoods

Crucially, the plan places job-creation at its heart. High-tech units tend to bring in more than just workers—they demand engineers, designers, technicians, apprentices. That means local youth can stay home and build futures. The article asserts “high-tech employment, investment growth and industrial transformation” will result.

Inviting investments & resources

The announcement emphasises inviting entrepreneurs and investors—especially those from Bihar who have made their mark elsewhere—to bring industries home.
Plus, public-sector giants (Maharatna, Navratna companies) will deploy industry units, offering credibility, scale and resource-backing.

The Road Ahead: What Needs to Happen

Infrastructure must match ambition

Even the best plans falter when infrastructure lags. To succeed, these clusters will require reliable power, clean water, good transport, and skilled manpower. The announcement acknowledges as much—”industrial corridors, high-quality power supply, water management and skilled human resources are necessary.” 
Hence, the state must ensure road-maps are laid out, timelines fixed and accountability visible.

Skill-building & education

A cluster is only as good as its workforce. Bihar already flagged an AI-education initiative for students under CM Nitish earlier this year, showing the direction. 
Now, bridging school, college and industry must become seamless: so that youth can walk from graduation straight into tech labs, not migrate away.

Sustained policy, not headline promises

Announcements are vital—but execution will define outcomes. The state must maintain favourable policy, ease of doing business, and consistent support across political cycles. In other words: this can’t fade after the headlines.

What It Means for You and Me

If you’re a young person in Bihar, a parent, a local entrepreneur or community member—this is more than news. It can translate into opportunity. You may no longer need to leave Bihar to seek high-end jobs. New workshops, design labs, chip-units might open near you.
If you’re an investor or entrepreneur with roots in Bihar: here’s a signal to come home, re-invest talent, resources and ambitions.
And for all of us who think of Bihar in traditional terms—it’s time to reimagine. The state is signalling it can be tech-strong, industrially capable, and globally competitive.

Why This Story Should Be Told

Because stories shape perception. Because for too long, Bihar’s narrative has centred on migration, under-employment and opportunity-loss. This is a story of turnaround, of where the young might stay and build their future.
That is precisely why we at Bihar Say share it. We believe Bihar’s next story is one of transformation—of tech-hubs, innovation, and rooted talent.

content:
The Journey Home Made Easy

As the fourth day of the vibrant Chhath Puja (which concludes on 28 October) draws to a close, many festival-goers in Bihar are preparing to head back to their workplaces in other states. According to reports, 8 special trains will be deployed to ease this massive movement of people. These services aim to connect Bihar with major hubs like Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru and towns in Gujarat.

Why These 8 Special Trains Matter

First, the holiday rush after a major festival often leads to congestion, long queues and uncertain travel. Secondly, many travellers find regular trains full or difficult to book. With dedicated special trains, travellers gain better access — including sleepers, general and AC coaches.
Notably, these trains will begin operations from 28 October onwards on various routes, thereby enabling smoother return journeys from Bihar. According to local media, they will especially benefit passengers in North Bihar.

Which Trains Will Run?

Here are the 8 trains announced:

  • Train No. 04651: Jayanagar → Amritsar (Special)

  • Train No. 04097: Hasanpur Road → New Delhi (Special)

  • Train No. 04732: Samastipur → Sriganganagar (Special)

  • Train No. 04449: Darbhanga → New Delhi (Special)

  • Train No. 07358: Raxaul → UBL (Bengaluru) Special

  • Train No. 05557: Raxaul → LTT (Mumbai) Special

  • Train No. 09068: Jayanagar → Udhna Special

  • Train No. 09070: Samastipur → Udhna Special

By introducing these routes, the rail network expands relief and return-options for those heading back to metros and industrial hubs.

What to Keep in Mind Before Boarding

  • Book early: Seats are limited and with the festival rush, availability drops fast.

  • Check class options: These specials include AC, Sleeper and General—so pick what suits you.

  • Routes and timings: They vary by origin and destination; verify schedule ahead of travel.

  • Extra coaches may be added: Officials say extra coaches will be attached if demand surges.

  • Plan arrival to main hubs: Whether you’re going to Delhi, Mumbai or Bengaluru, ensure onward connectivity.

Why This Move Matters for Bihar Travellers

By launching these specials, the railways recognise the massive travel demand from Bihar during Chhath and other festivals. For many from Bihar working in metro cities, the return journey often is fraught with uncertainty. Thanks to this move:

  • It offers better connectivity between Bihar and major employment centres.

  • It shows a responsive transport policy, matching travel peak with supply.

  • It helps families return home, celebrate, and then go back without undue delay.
