content:
IIT Patna and Amity University Collaborate to Transform Teacher Education

Patna is witnessing a remarkable step in teacher education. IIT Patna and Amity University Patna have officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate under the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP) sponsored by the University Grants Commission (UGC). This partnership promises to empower teachers with advanced skills, research opportunities, and innovative training aligned with National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

The MoU was signed by Prof. T. N. Singh, Director of IIT Patna, and Prof. (Dr.) Vivekanand Pandey, Vice Chancellor of Amity University Patna. The event gathered senior faculty members, officials, and the Program Director of MMTTC at IIT Patna, reflecting a strong commitment to improving teacher quality and higher education in Bihar.

Focus on Research, Innovation, and Practical Learning

According to Prof. T. N. Singh, this collaboration will integrate research and innovation into teacher training programs. He emphasized that the initiative will not only benefit educators in Bihar but also create ripple effects across India. Furthermore, the MoU encourages practical learning and introduces contemporary teaching methods, helping educators make meaningful contributions to society.

Transitioning from traditional training, teachers will now gain access to cutting-edge workshops, seminars, and research projects. These initiatives will enhance the quality of education delivered in classrooms and prepare teachers to handle diverse learning environments efficiently.

Empowering Faculty and Elevating Excellence

Prof. (Dr.) Vivekanand Pandey highlighted that the partnership will focus on faculty empowerment. Joint curriculum improvements and collaborative research projects will foster continuous learning for educators. In addition, these efforts aim to create an ecosystem of innovation, where teachers can implement creative strategies and actively participate in educational reforms.

The MoU ensures structured opportunities for teachers to enhance their professional development. Moreover, it strengthens Bihar’s position as a hub for high-quality education and teacher training. Students, in turn, benefit directly from better-trained educators equipped to meet modern learning demands.

Workshops, Seminars, and Continuous Learning

One of the key pillars of this collaboration includes organizing joint workshops and seminars. These platforms will allow educators to share insights, explore new teaching methodologies, and engage in meaningful dialogue. Additionally, the partnership encourages research collaborations to address real-world challenges in education.

By focusing on continuous learning and innovation, IIT Patna and Amity University are setting a new benchmark for teacher training programs. This initiative aligns perfectly with the broader goals of NEP 2020 and ensures a modern, effective, and practical approach to teaching.

Join the Movement of Educational Transformation in Bihar

IIT Patna and Amity University Patna are leading the charge to reshape teacher education in Bihar. With this MoU, educators can access innovative resources, research-driven programs, and collaborative learning opportunities.

content:
Patna Sahib to Glow with 11,000 Diyas This Diwali – A Unique Eco-Friendly Celebration at Takht Shri Harmandir

Patna Sahib to Shine with 11,000 Diyas This Diwali – Celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas in an Eco-Friendly Way

A Bandi Chhor Divas Like Never Before

This year, Patna Sahib will witness a spectacular celebration as Takht Shri Harmandir is lit with 11,000 diyas for Bandi Chhor Divas. The festival isn’t just about lights; it’s a conscious effort to promote eco-friendly celebrations and environmental awareness. Devotees from across India are preparing with excitement to be part of this unique event.

Eco-Friendly Diwali Initiative

The gurudwara management committee has introduced an innovative approach to this year’s celebrations. All 11,000 diyas are traditional clay lamps, reducing environmental impact. The initiative encourages communities to celebrate Diwali sustainably, spreading a powerful message of green living alongside devotion.

Religious Significance

Bandi Chhor Divas marks the historic release of Guru Hargobind Sahib, the sixth Sikh Guru, from Gwalior Fort by Emperor Jahangir. Guru Sahib also freed 52 other kings, demonstrating compassion and justice. Since then, Sikhs commemorate this day by lighting diyas, praying, and holding community gatherings, blending history and spiritual devotion.

Special Programs at Takht Shri Harmandir

On Bandi Chhor Divas, Takht Shri Harmandir will host bhajan-kirtan, spiritual discourses, and a special langar for devotees. Sikh families from all over India participate, creating a vibrant and united celebration that highlights the festival’s religious and cultural significance.

Tradition of Diyas at Home

Families bring a lit diya from their home to the gurudwara, then light all other diyas at home with it. This sacred flame is believed to bring happiness, prosperity, and peace. Homes are also decorated with rangoli, adding color and joy to the festival.

Join the Celebration

Be part of this eco-friendly Bandi Chhor Divas and witness Takht Shri Harmandir illuminated by 11,000 diyas. Carry the flame of devotion and awareness back to your home, and celebrate tradition sustainably.

content:
“Every Second Counts”: AIIMS Patna Leads Bihar’s Fight Against Stroke with ‘Stroke Update 2025’

When every second decides between life and paralysis, AIIMS Patna is rewriting Bihar’s healthcare story.
With its bold step, “Stroke Update 2025,” the institute has launched a movement to bring speed, science, and hope to stroke patients across the state.

AIIMS Patna’s Landmark Initiative: Stroke Update 2025

The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Patna has introduced a transformative program to change stroke care in Bihar.
Titled “Stroke Update 2025,” the initiative focuses on rapid diagnosis, timely treatment, and collaboration between experts—three elements that can save lives when time is short.

Jointly organized by the Departments of Neurology and Neurosurgery, the event was inaugurated by Prof. (Brig.) Dr. Raju Agarwal, Director of AIIMS Patna.
During the event, he announced the creation of a dedicated Acute Stroke Care Unit—a specialized facility designed to deliver immediate, evidence-based care.

“Timely intervention is the key to preserving life and neurological function,” said Prof. Agarwal, urging hospitals to act faster than ever before.

Acute Stroke Care Unit: Where Time Meets Technology

The upcoming Acute Stroke Care Unit will handle thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy, two procedures that can reverse brain damage if done quickly.
This development ensures that patients in Bihar receive world-class treatment without delays.

Prof. Vikas Chandra Jha, Head of Neurosurgery, shared crucial insights.
Nearly 80% of strokes in India are ischemic and can be treated if addressed in time.
He also pointed to the alarming rise in strokes among younger adults, calling for stronger emergency systems and awareness campaigns.

Uniting Experts for Faster Response and Better Recovery

The event brought together more than 200 experts, including neurologists, neurosurgeons, and general physicians from AIIMS, PMCH, IGIMS, and regional hospitals.
Through discussions on emergency triage, rehabilitation, and neurointervention, the program inspired collaboration across Bihar’s healthcare network.

Additionally, the speakers emphasized ambulance-based rapid response models and the need to expand stroke-ready hospitals throughout the state.
The initiative also aligns with the National Health Programme’s mission to strengthen critical care in every district.

Beyond Treatment: Building a Future of Compassion and Innovation

For AIIMS Patna, this is not just a hospital project—it’s a promise of progress.
The institute aims to create a statewide stroke network, connecting rural and urban Bihar under one efficient care system.

“Stroke Update 2025 is a milestone in neurological care. It reflects AIIMS Patna’s commitment to innovation, compassion, and clinical excellence,” said Prof. Jha, expressing hope for a healthier and more aware Bihar.

content:
ECI Declares Paid Holiday for All Bihar Employees on Polling Days — Empowering Every Voter

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has taken a strong step to boost voter turnout in Bihar. It has announced that all employees in the state, including daily and casual workers, will get a paid holiday on polling days during the upcoming General Assembly elections and bye-elections across eight constituencies.

This proactive move aims to remove one of the biggest hurdles in voting — work commitments — and ensure that every eligible citizen gets the time and freedom to vote.

Mark the Polling Dates and Plan Ahead

The ECI wants citizens to prepare early for the elections.

  • Phase I: November 6, 2025 (Thursday)

  • Phase II and Bye-Elections: November 11, 2025 (Tuesday)

By giving this clarity well in advance, the Commission hopes voters will plan their day and make voting a priority rather than an afterthought.

Legal Protection Under Section 135B

The decision comes under Section 135B of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which legally requires employers to grant a paid holiday to every employee who is entitled to vote.

If an employer denies this right or deducts wages for the day, strict action can follow. The ECI’s clear message is simple — voting is not just a right, it’s a protected duty.

Who Benefits from This Initiative

This paid holiday extends far beyond government offices.
It includes:

  • Public and Private Sector Employees

  • Daily Wage and Casual Workers

  • Employees Working Outside Their Constituency but Registered in Bihar

Even those working in industrial or commercial establishments outside their voting area can now take leave without losing pay. This ensures that no voter is left behind.

Strengthening Democracy, One Vote at a Time

By ensuring that financial worries do not stop people from voting, the ECI is strengthening democracy at the grassroots. Many voters, especially those from the informal sector, often skip voting due to the fear of wage loss.

Now, with paid leave guaranteed, every individual can contribute to shaping Bihar’s political future.

Moreover, this decision reflects how institutions like the Election Commission of India are actively promoting inclusive participation in elections — not just by urging people to vote, but by removing barriers that stop them.

Patna Welcomes 166 Extra Flights for Diwali & Chhath Puja

This festive season, Patna is set to become the travel hotspot of Bihar. Air India and its subsidiary Air India Express have announced a massive addition of 166 extra flights to meet soaring travel demand during Diwali and Chhath Puja. Consequently, passengers traveling from key cities like Delhi, Mumbai, and Bengaluru can now enjoy more convenient schedules and smoother connections.

The additional flights begin operations October 15, 2025, and continue until November 3, 2025. Therefore, travelers should plan early to secure their seats and avoid last-minute hassles.

Air India: Expanded Routes and Numbers

Air India will operate 114 additional flights to Patna. Specifically:

  • Delhi–Patna: 38 extra flights

  • Mumbai–Patna: 38 extra flights

  • Bengaluru–Patna: 38 extra flights

Moreover, these flights complement the existing 42 weekly Air India flights from Delhi and Mumbai. As a result, passengers have more flexibility to choose their preferred travel times.

Air India Express Enhances Festive Connectivity

Similarly, Air India Express adds 52 flights between October 22 and November 3, 2025:

  • Delhi–Patna: 26 additional flights

  • Bengaluru–Patna: 26 additional flights

Additionally, these flights supplement the current 14 weekly Air India Express flights. Therefore, the festive travel rush is expected to ease considerably, offering passengers more convenient options.

Smooth Connections to Domestic and International Destinations

Furthermore, these additional flights not only boost domestic connectivity but also facilitate seamless transfers to international destinations via Delhi, Mumbai, and Bengaluru hubs. Consequently, travelers heading to the Middle East or Europe can coordinate layovers efficiently.

This expansion is particularly helpful for Biharis living abroad who wish to celebrate Diwali and Chhath with their families. Indeed, the move reflects the airlines’ commitment to serving passengers’ festive travel needs while minimizing congestion and delays.

How to Book Your Festive Flight

Booking for these flights is now open through multiple channels:

  1. Official websites and mobile apps of Air India and Air India Express

  2. 24×7 contact centres

  3. City and airport ticketing offices

  4. Travel agents worldwide

Hence, passengers can choose the most convenient booking method and ensure a smooth festive journey.

How DeHaat Transformed 1.8 Million Farmer Lives in Just 13 Years: The Story of Bihar's AgriTech Giant

From Fields to Fortune: How DeHaat Transformed 1.8 Million Farmer Lives in Just 13 YearsSeries: 60 Days – 60 Startups from Bihar | Presented by Bihar Say

“मिट्टी से निकली कहानी, जिसने लाखों ज़िंदगियों की फसल बदल दी।”Some stories don’t begin in boardrooms. They rise from dust, driven by patience, persistence, and a purpose rooted in rural India.

The Humble Seed That Sprouted a Movement (2012–2025)

Who is Founder of DeHaat

In 2012, four young visionaries—Shashank Kumar, Amrendra Singh, Adarsh Srivastava, and Shyam Sundar Singh—stood at a crossroads. They could have taken high-paying jobs or joined global firms, but something called them back home to Bihar.

What they saw there was deeply personal. Across villages, farmers struggled with poor-quality seeds, erratic pricing, and outdated advice. Many had no access to reliable credit or markets. And most of all, they had no one to turn to when things went wrong.

This broken agricultural chain sparked an idea. Instead of watching from the sidelines, the founders stepped in. With degrees from IIT Delhi, IIT Kharagpur, and IIM Ahmedabad, they launched DeHaat™—a grassroots platform designed to make agriculture fairer, smarter, and more inclusive.

From One Village to Millions: Scaling a Vision State by State

What started in a handful of Bihari districts has grown into one of India’s most impactful agri-tech networks. DeHaat now serves 1.8 million farmers across 12 Indian states.

This reach wasn’t accidental. At the core of their model lies the DeHaat Center—a local hub run by trained micro-entrepreneurs. These centers offer farmers everything from high-quality seeds and fertilizers to market access and AI-based advisory services.

The numbers are impressive: over 11,000 centers and 503 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) form a backbone that supports rural livelihoods. But the real impact goes beyond metrics.

Consider a farmer from Begusarai who once relied on middlemen and now directly sells his harvest at competitive prices. Or a mother of two in Nalanda who runs a DeHaat Center, helping 300 farmers grow sustainably while earning respect in her community.

Stories like these define DeHaat’s legacy—one farmer at a time, one season at a time.

When AI Speaks the Farmer’s Language

Technology often fails when it forgets its audience. DeHaat understood this early.

That’s why their AI-powered advisory system doesn’t just crunch data—it speaks the language of the land. Whether it’s Bhojpuri, Maithili, Magahi, or Hindi, farmers receive updates tailored to their region and crop cycle.

This system now offers predictive insights for more than 30 crops, guiding farmers through weather shifts, pest risks, and soil health management. The goal isn’t to replace intuition—it’s to strengthen it with science.

Such integration of technology and tradition hasn’t gone unnoticed. DeHaat has been recognized by NITI Aayog, NASSCOM, Forbes, ET, and even the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation for its scalable, inclusive model.

A Culture That Mirrors the Soil It Serves

DeHaat’s internal values reflect its external mission. They don’t just build systems for farmers—they build a culture that understands the value of every contributor.

Mutual respect drives communication, whether it’s among colleagues or with farmers. Accountability and ownership aren’t buzzwords—they’re practiced daily, from the field to the boardroom. And when it comes to diversity, DeHaat doesn’t just talk inclusion—it lives it.

Their team includes voices from various castes, genders, religions, and regions. Celebrations are plural, hiring is inclusive, and feedback is welcomed from all levels.

For two consecutive years—2022 and 2023—DeHaat earned the Great Place to Work certification. This recognition didn’t come from perks, but from purpose—shared by hundreds of employees who believe in the mission and each other.

Not Just a Startup. A Soil-Born Movement.

Labels don’t define DeHaat. It is more than a startup, more than a success story. It is a quiet revolution powered by local dreams and national urgency.

The team didn’t set out to disrupt. They set out to repair. To restore pride to farming. To rebuild trust in rural economies. And to remind India that the future doesn’t only bloom in metros—it also sprouts in villages.

From the soil of Bihar to the farms of Maharashtra and beyond, DeHaat has proven one thing:The farmer doesn’t need charity. The farmer needs access, dignity, and opportunity.

And DeHaat is determined to keep delivering all three.

That vision gave birth to GoFloww, a SaaS startup focused not on tech giants, but on the millions of overlooked MSMEs (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises) spread across India.

GoFloww: A SaaS Solution Rooted in India’s Reality

Founded in 2020, GoFloww builds modular, easy-to-use business tools tailored for Indian entrepreneurs. These aren’t sleek products designed in boardrooms and tested in cities. They’re simple, purpose-driven solutions crafted for small business owners in towns like Saharsa, Ballia, and Madhepura—who have never hired an IT person but still dream of scaling up.

Meet the Founders: Anish & Prakhar Kumar Singh

Behind GoFloww are Anish Kumar Singh and Prakhar Kumar Singh, both IIT Bombay graduates. But their story doesn’t start with venture capital or accelerators. Instead, it begins with countless conversations with small business owners—mechanics, coaching centre heads, cloth sellers—struggling with attendance logs, invoices, and client communication.

They weren’t looking for flashy dashboards. They just wanted clarity, consistency, and affordable digital tools.

The founders decided to build where the gap was widest—not in the market, but in access. That’s how GoFloww became a company designed with empathy, built for Bharat, and operated from Bihar.

Atom Suite: Tools Designed for Everyday Business Challenges

Each product functions as a standalone tool. Users can subscribe to what fits their need and budget. This structure ensures that even the smallest businesses can begin their digital journey without heavy investment or technical support.

Scaling Slowly, Building Deeply: Impact Across 1,000+ MSMEs

Over the last three years, GoFloww has quietly expanded its footprint. More than 1,000 MSMEs across India now use one or more of its tools.

What’s more compelling is the type of user base—businesses from districts and towns where tech often arrives last. For them, GoFloww isn’t just software. It’s a first step into a structured, scalable business operation.

And while the company has earned features in YourStory, India Today, and Hindustan, its real validation comes from entrepreneurs who now spend less time managing chaos and more time growing their businesses.

The Bihar Advantage: Grounded Innovation

Being based in Patna, GoFloww doesn’t follow the usual SaaS script. It writes its own.

The choice to stay in Bihar was intentional. It meant being closer to the challenges they wanted to solve. It allowed for better cost control, enabling them to offer entry-level access to their tools at minimal pricing. But more importantly, it gave them insight into the daily digital struggles of Indian MSMEs.

Unlike startups shaped by investor decks, GoFloww is shaped by field calls, feedback, and the occasional chai-stall consultation.

A Different Kind of Digital Transformation

GoFloww isn’t claiming to solve everything. It’s not building the next unicorn. But it is building something rare—a set of tools that lets small business owners work smarter, without feeling left out of the digital revolution.

Their story proves that tech can be inclusive if you build it with the right intent, in the right place, and for the right people.

Sumant Sinha: Founder of ReNew Power and Bihar's Green Energy Pioneer

“Sumant Sinha of ReNew Power – Bihar’s ₹3,000 Crore Green Energy Visionary”

“Bihar has always produced leaders — but in today’s era, one man from the state is powering not just homes, but India’s clean energy future: Sumant Sinha.”

Who is Sumant Sinha?

Born into a family known for public service, Sumant Sinha is the son of Yashwant Sinha, India’s former Finance Secretary and Union Minister. Unlike his father, who chose politics and administration, Sumant carved a different path. He entered the corporate world with a focus on energy, finance, and business leadership.

Educated at IIT Delhi and Columbia University, Sumant developed a rare mix of technical knowledge and financial expertise. This combination later became the backbone of his success in the renewable energy industry.

Before starting his own venture, he held senior positions at Aditya Birla Group and Suzlon Energy, gaining both global exposure and sectoral insight. However, it was his entrepreneurial leap that changed everything.

ReNew Power – Sumant Sinha’s Green Revolution

In 2011, Sumant Sinha founded ReNew Power with a clear mission: to make renewable energy mainstream in India. At a time when many companies still relied on coal and oil, his idea looked risky. But his vision was strong — India needed clean power for sustainable growth.

Today, ReNew Power has grown into India’s largest renewable energy company. With projects in solar and wind power across states, it has become a household name in sustainability. Under Sumant’s leadership, the company attracted global investors and established itself as a pioneer in India’s fight against climate change.

Sumant Sinha’s Net Worth and Lifestyle

With his wealth crossing ₹3,000 crore, Sumant ranks among the richest green business leaders from Bihar. But unlike many billionaires, his lifestyle reflects his values. He is often seen in premium electric vehicles, choosing eco-friendly options even in his personal life.

This balance of business success and personal responsibility has earned him respect not just in corporate circles, but also among climate advocates worldwide.

Family Roots and Bihar Connection

Being the son of Yashwant Sinha gave Sumant exposure to leadership early on. But instead of politics, he found his calling in energy. His journey is a reminder that Bihar’s sons and daughters can achieve greatness in modern, global industries.

He proudly represents Bihar in global forums, redefining the narrative of a state often known only for migration or underdevelopment. Through his story, Bihar gains a new identity — one of innovation and sustainability.

ReNew Power and India’s Clean Energy Future

Under Sumant Sinha, ReNew Power is not only a company but also a model for India’s green growth. It has reduced carbon emissions by millions of tonnes, created thousands of jobs, and set global benchmarks.

As the world moves toward net-zero goals, leaders like Sumant prove that business growth and climate action can go hand in hand. His journey inspires young entrepreneurs to dream big while staying responsible.

Bihar Wants Your Ideas—Are You Ready to Step Up?

From village classrooms to city cafés, innovation lives everywhere in Bihar. And now, the state government wants to hear from you.

This is more than just a portal. It’s a signal that Bihar is ready to listen, support, and scale ideas that can transform lives.

What Is the Bihar Idea Festival?

The Bihar Idea Festival is a first-of-its-kind initiative by the Department of Industries, in association with JEEViKA and other partners. Its mission is to collect more than 10,000 innovative ideas from all 38 districts of Bihar.

Instead of chasing innovation in urban centres alone, the portal focuses on grassroots entrepreneurship. It invites solutions for local challenges—from sustainable farming to health tech, from education tools to rural business models.

For decades, bright minds from Bihar have migrated to other states, seeking platforms to express their ideas. This portal changes that narrative. Now, the government is bringing the platform home, inviting innovation from every corner of the state.

Importantly, it represents a shift in how policy engages with people—from top-down direction to bottom-up participation. With the right support, even small ideas from rural Bihar can become engines of growth.

content:
Gomini: India's First Cow Care Startup Blending Tradition & Technology

In April 2025, two men from Bihar decided to do something that sounded almost impossible—help people in big cities own a cow.

At first, the idea seemed strange. How could someone living in a busy apartment in Delhi or Mumbai ever think of having an indigenous cow? But for Dr. Arjun Sharma and Gauri Shankar, this wasn’t just about milk. It was about restoring a bond India has slowly been losing—the sacred connection between humans, cows, and the village way of life.

And so, Gomini was born—India’s first managed cow care service platform, headquartered in Bihar.

Gomini Founders Dr. Arjun Sharma and Gauri Shankar: Remembering Their Roots

Both founders grew up seeing how deeply cows were woven into everyday rural life. They weren’t just animals; they were part of the family, symbols of prosperity, purity, and spiritual strength.

But in cities, that bond was fading. Modern families, caught in the rush of deadlines and traffic, were losing touch with this living heritage. Dr. Sharma and Shankar wanted to change that.

They asked a simple yet powerful question:“What if every urban family could own a cow without leaving their city, while also giving rural women a chance to earn with dignity?”

How Gomini Blends Tradition With Technology

The idea took shape as Gomini, launched in April 2025. Here, an urban family can “own” an indigenous cow while a trained caretaker—usually a rural woman or farmer—takes care of it on their farm.

For the family, it means:

Pure A2 milk they can trust Panchagavya wellness products rooted in Indian traditions Access to village life experiences like cow worship, rural crafts, and spiritual retreats

Pure A2 milk they can trust

Panchagavya wellness products rooted in Indian traditions

Access to village life experiences like cow worship, rural crafts, and spiritual retreats

For the caretaker, it means financial independence, respect, and empowerment.

But Gomini did not stop at tradition—it brought in technology:

Each cow is RFID-tagged and linked to an NFT, ensuring lifelong ownership records IoT and AI systems track health and detect stress early CCTV live streams connect families to their cows in real time Soon, augmented reality will allow virtual interaction with cows from anywhere in the world

Each cow is RFID-tagged and linked to an NFT, ensuring lifelong ownership records

IoT and AI systems track health and detect stress early

CCTV live streams connect families to their cows in real time

Soon, augmented reality will allow virtual interaction with cows from anywhere in the world

It’s an extraordinary blend of heritage and high-tech, creating trust and emotional connection.

Dr. Arjun Sharma’s Vision for Cow-Centric Villages

The larger dream of Dr. Arjun Sharma and Gauri Shankar is to build cow-centric villages. As herds grow, each village could house 500 cows, turning into:

Organic farming hubs free from chemicals Self-reliant ecosystems Employment engines for women and farmers Sustainability models aligned with the United Nations’ global goals

Organic farming hubs free from chemicals

Self-reliant ecosystems

Employment engines for women and farmers

Sustainability models aligned with the United Nations’ global goals

In Dr. Sharma’s words:

“With Gomini, we aim to bring prosperity home by restoring the cultural, ecological, and economic significance of India’s indigenous cows. We want to reconnect urban families to their roots while empowering rural women with dignity.”

“With Gomini, we aim to bring prosperity home by restoring the cultural, ecological, and economic significance of India’s indigenous cows. We want to reconnect urban families to their roots while empowering rural women with dignity.”

Bihar Startup Gomini Inspires a New Movement

Today, the Gomini app is live on Google Play Store and Apple App Store, already gaining interest from families across India. What started as a dream in Bihar is now inspiring a cultural revival, using cows as the bridge between cities and villages.

This is not just a startup story. It’s a story of roots and modernity walking hand in hand, showing how Bihar’s entrepreneurs are reshaping India’s future—one cow, one village, one family at a time.

title: Discover India’s Oldest Functional Temple: Mundeshwari, Bihar’s 2000-Year-Old Wonder!
summary: Tucked away in the Kaimur Hills of Bihar, the 2000-year-old Mundeshwari Temple is India's oldest continuously functional temple featuring a rare octagonal design.
content:
Discover India’s Oldest Functional Temple: Mundeshwari, Bihar’s 2000-Year-Old Wonder!

Do you know the oldest temple in India?

Most might guess Kashi or Ayodhya, but no—it’s Mundeshwari Temple, tucked away in the breathtaking Kaimur Hills of Bihar! This architectural gem, believed to have been built during the Gupta period, is over 2,000 years old and still stands as one of the oldest continuously functional temples in the world.

A 2000-Year-Old Marvel of Faith and History

Perched majestically atop the Kaimur Hills, Mundeshwari Temple is dedicated to Goddess Mundeshwari and Lord Shiva. The unique octagonal design of the temple is a rare architectural feat, setting it apart from other ancient temples.

This geometric design symbolizes not only artistic ingenuity but also ancient tantric traditions that thrived here centuries ago.

The rituals at Mundeshwari have remained unbroken for thousands of years, making it a living testament to India’s spiritual heritage. Every stone in the temple seems to echo stories of devotion, resilience, and timeless traditions. Stepping inside feels like walking into a historical time capsule, where the aura of ancient India still lingers.

What Makes Mundeshwari Temple Unique?

  • Octagonal Architecture: Unlike most temples with rectangular or square layouts, Mundeshwari’s rare octagonal design is awe-inspiring and deeply symbolic.
  • Tantric Roots: The temple showcases the rich tantric history of India, blending it seamlessly with Vedic rituals.
  • Continuous Worship: Mundeshwari is one of the few temples in the world where rituals have been practiced uninterrupted for centuries.

A Journey Back in Time

Mundeshwari Temple is not just a spiritual hub but also a heritage site that showcases the richness of Indian history. Nestled amid scenic hills, the journey to this temple is as rewarding as the destination. For history enthusiasts, architecture lovers, or spiritual seekers, visiting this temple offers a profound connection to the past.

Plan your visit to Mundeshwari and witness the confluence of history, architecture, and spirituality.

title: Bihar’s Sabhyata Dwar: Monumental Symbol of Cultural Unity and Heritage
summary: Standing 32 meters high on the banks of the Ganga in Patna, Sabhyata Dwar honors Bihar's Mauryan architectural glory and ancient civilizational heritage.
content:
Bihar’s Sabhyata Dwar: Monumental Symbol of Cultural Unity and Heritage

Republic Day evokes pride and unity all over India. But in Bihar, it’s especially significant.

The Sabhyata Dwar in Patna stands as a monumental tribute to Bihar’s rich cultural and architectural history. It reminds us of our heritage and the enduring values that shaped our nation.

The Story of Sabhyata Dwar: A Monument of Pride

Sabhyata Dwar, also known as the “Gateway of Civilization,” rises proudly near the banks of the Ganga River in Patna. Built to honor Bihar’s cultural and historical contributions, the design draws deep inspiration from the Mauryan and Ashokan Empire, with elements reflecting peace, knowledge, and civilizational progress.

Standing at an impressive 32 meters, the structure is crafted from fine red and beige sandstone sourced from Rajasthan. Its arches and pillars resemble the Sanchi Stupa and Ashokan edicts, featuring intricate carvings that emphasize Bihar’s spiritual and intellectual heritage, connecting us directly to the roots of Buddhism and Jainism.

Why Sabhyata Dwar Matters for Bihar's Heritage

Sabhyata Dwar is more than just a monument. It symbolizes the timeless values of equality, justice, and democracy that originated in the ancient republic of Vaishali and the imperial capital of Pataliputra.

This monument blends ancient history with modern Bihari pride. For residents, it serves as a daily reminder of our illustrious roots. For visitors from across the globe, it offers a breathtaking gateway into Bihar’s civilizational legacy.

Why You Should Visit Sabhyata Dwar

Visiting Sabhyata Dwar on the Ganga waterfront offers a unique cultural experience. You can explore its stunning carvings, walk through its peaceful landscaped surroundings, and reflect on Bihar’s profound contributions to philosophy, governance, and world history.
